extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies and agency employees (standards executives, procurement and regulatory staff, and agency participants in standards bodies); NIST and OMB staff
extracted.subtask_description: OMB Circular (A-119) guidance on when and how federal agencies must use, reference, participate in, manage, and report on technical standards (voluntary consensus, non-consensus, government-unique, and legally-mandated standards) in procurement and regulation. Covers definitions, participation principles, reporting procedures, and agency responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory use of voluntary consensus standards
rubrics_metrics.description: All federal agencies must use voluntary consensus standards in lieu of government-unique standards in their procurement and regulatory activities, except where inconsistent with law or otherwise impractical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an agency determines use would be inconsistent with law or impractical, the head of the agency must transmit an explanation to OMB through NIST (see reporting requirements in Section 9). Agencies retain discretion to decline use if inconsistent with law or impractical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The term standard (or technical standard) includes common and repeated use of rules, conditions, guidelines or characteristics for products or related processes and production methods, related management systems practices; definition of terms; classification of components; delineation of procedures; specification of dimensions, materials, performance, designs, or operations; measurement of quality and quantity; test methods and sampling procedures; descriptions of fit and measurements of size or strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term does not include professional standards of personal conduct or institutional codes of ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of performance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A performance standard states requirements in terms of required results with criteria for verifying compliance but without stating the methods for achieving required results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A performance standard may define functional, operational, and/or interface and interchangeability characteristics and is contrasted with a prescriptive standard that specifies design requirements, materials, or methods of fabrication or construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of non-government standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-government standard is a standardization document developed by a private sector association, organization, or technical society which plans, develops, establishes, or coordinates standards, specifications, handbooks, or related documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and attributes of voluntary consensus standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary consensus standards are standards developed or adopted by voluntary consensus standards bodies and include provisions for making relevant IP available on a non-discriminatory, royalty-free or reasonable royalty basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attributes of voluntary consensus standards bodies include openness; balance of interest; due process; an appeals process; and consensus (general agreement, not necessarily unanimity) with procedures for resolving objections, advising objectors of dispositions and reasons, and opportunity to change votes after reviewing comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other types of standards (non-consensus, government-unique, statutory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-consensus/industry/company/de facto standards are developed in the private sector but not through full consensus; government-unique standards are developed by the government for its own uses; standards mandated by law (e.g., USP/NF) are distinct categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Use' of a standard
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Use' means incorporation of a standard in whole, in part, or by reference for procurement purposes, and inclusion of a standard in whole, in part, or by reference in regulation(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Impractical' for non-use
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Impractical' includes circumstances in which use would fail to serve agency program needs; would be infeasible; would be inadequate, ineffectual, inefficient, or inconsistent with agency mission; or would impose more burdens or be less useful than use of another standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency must report use of government-unique standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must report to NIST by December 31 each year decisions in the previous fiscal year to use government-unique standards instead of voluntary consensus standards; no report required if no voluntary consensus standard exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report must include explanation of reasons why use of a voluntary consensus standard would be inconsistent with law or impractical, and follow NIST format instructions (see Sections 11b(2), 12a(3), and 12b(2) references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency must report participation in standards bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must report annually to NIST information on the nature and extent of agency participation in development and use of voluntary consensus standards from the previous fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items include number of standards bodies with agency participation and number of agency employees participating; number of voluntary consensus standards the agency has used since last report; identification of standards substituted for government-unique standards as a result of review; and an evaluation of policy effectiveness and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency process to manage and report standards use
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency must establish a process to identify, manage, and review its development and use of standards, with the ability to report to OMB through NIST on use of government-unique standards (with explanations) and participation in voluntary consensus standards development and use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy establishes two reporting methods—category-based and transaction-based—and agencies must report all uses of standards in one or both ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for reporting standards in regulations (transaction-based reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency issues regulations that use or reference standards, it should use transaction-based reporting and must follow procedures when issuing or revising a regulation that contains a standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures include publishing requests for comment in the preamble of an NPRM or IFR with specific statements (see next entries) and publishing discussion in the final rule preamble that restates NPRM statements, summarizes and responds to comments, and explains final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: NPRM preamble disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposing a regulation: (1) if proposing to use a voluntary consensus standard, identify it; (2) if proposing to use a government-unique standard instead, identify it and give a preliminary explanation for doing so; (3) if using a government-unique standard and no voluntary consensus standard has been identified, so state and invite identification of any such standard and explanations why it should be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure must be published in the preamble of the NPRM or IFR to solicit comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rule preamble disclosure and response requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In the final rule preamble, restate the NPRM/IFR statement(s), acknowledge and summarize comments received, respond to them, and explain the agency's final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using a voluntary consensus standard, identify it and any alternative voluntary standards identified. When using a government-unique standard in lieu of a voluntary consensus standard, identify the standards and explain why use of the voluntary consensus standard would be inconsistent with law or impractical, and transmit that explanation per Section 9a. If no voluntary consensus standard exists, state that.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for reporting standards use in procurements (category or transaction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must report the standards used in procurements either on a categorical basis or on a transaction basis and must report all uses in one or both ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice depends on procurement patterns: category-based for large/recurring gov-unique use; transaction-based for mostly commercial procurements with occasional gov-unique use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-based procurement reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting on a category basis, agencies must maintain a centralized standards management system, systematically review government-unique standards for conversion to voluntary consensus standards, maintain records of categories using government-unique standards with explanations, and enable potential offerors to suggest voluntary consensus standards as replacements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This method is useful for large procurements or long-term contracts requiring replacement parts based on government-unique standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transaction-based procurement reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting on a transaction basis, each solicitation referencing government-unique standards must identify those standards and provide offerors an opportunity to suggest alternative voluntary consensus standards that meet the agency’s requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If suggestions are made and the agency still decides to use government-unique standards, the agency must explain in its report to OMB (per Section 9a) why the voluntary consensus standards would be inconsistent with law or impractical.

rubrics_metrics.name: COTS and private-sector-standards exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitations for commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) products, or for products or services that rely on voluntary consensus standards or non-consensus private sector standards, or products that do not rely on government-unique standards, are not subject to the procurement reporting requirements in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations when deciding whether to use a standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should take full account of effects on the economy and applicable federal laws and policies (antitrust, national security, small business, product safety, environment, metrication, technology development, conflicts of interest) when considering using a standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should recognize that improper use of standards can suppress competition, impede innovation, exclude safer or less expensive products, or adversely affect trade, commerce, health, or safety. If incorporating a standard into rulemaking, agencies must comply with Principles of Regulation (Section 1(b)) and other analytical requirements of Executive Order 12866.

rubrics_metrics.name: No preference between consensus and non-consensus private-sector standards
rubrics_metrics.description: This policy does not establish a preference among private-sector standards; agencies referencing non-consensus private-sector standards in regulations are not required to report on those actions and procurements based on non-consensus standards need not be reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may select non-consensus private-sector standards for establishing testing methods in regulation or choose among commercial-off-the-shelf products regardless of underlying standard development process.

rubrics_metrics.name: No preference between domestic and international voluntary consensus standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy does not establish a preference between domestic and international voluntary consensus standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, agencies should consider international standards in procurement and regulatory applications to promote trade and implement international treaty agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for performance standards when practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: When using voluntary consensus standards, agencies should give preference to performance standards when such standards can reasonably be used instead of prescriptive standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: How agencies should reference voluntary consensus standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should reference voluntary consensus standards, along with sources of availability, in appropriate publications, regulatory orders, and internal documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In regulations the reference must include the date of issuance. For other uses, agencies may omit the date if users are directed to the latest issue. When publishing a voluntary standard in an agency document, the agency must observe and protect the rights of the copyright holder and similar obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency participation policy in standards bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must consult with and participate in voluntary consensus standards bodies, domestic and international, when such consultation and participation is in the public interest and compatible with agency missions, authorities, priorities, and budget resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation is required when appropriate to increase likelihood standards meet public and private needs; see purposes and principles for participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposes of agency participation in standards bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency representatives should participate to eliminate the need for separate government-unique standards and to further national goals such as metrication, use of environmentally sound and energy-efficient materials/products/practices, and improvement of public health and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles limiting agency support
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency support for standards activities must be limited to activities that clearly further agency missions and priorities, be consistent with budget resources, and must not be contingent upon the outcome of the standards activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally federal support should not exceed that of other participants except where it is in the direct and predominant interest of the Government and timely development/revision appears unlikely without such support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of agency support permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency support may include direct financial support (grants, memberships, contracts), administrative support (travel costs, hosting meetings, secretarial functions), technical support (cooperative testing, agency personnel participation), joint planning with standards bodies, and participation of agency personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization and legal/ethical compliance for agency participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency employees participating in standards activities at government expense must be specifically authorized agency representatives and their participation must comply with applicable laws and regulations (including legal and budgetary authority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation as an officer, director, or trustee may raise significant ethics issues and agencies should involve their ethics officer before authorizing support or participation in such capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation does not imply agency endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency participation in voluntary consensus standards bodies does not necessarily connote agency agreement with or endorsement of decisions reached by such organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations for agency representatives' participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency representatives should participate actively and on an equal basis with other members in matters like establishing priorities, procedures, preparing/reviewing/approving standards, and developing/adopting new standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active participation includes full involvement in discussions and technical debates, registering opinions, and serving as chairpersons or in official capacities. Representatives may vote in accordance with bodies' procedures unless prohibited by law or agency policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations to maintain independence of standards bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency representatives must refrain from involvement in internal management of voluntary consensus standards bodies (selection of salaried officers/employees, establishment of staff salaries, administrative policies) and must not dominate such bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representatives are bound by bodies' rules and procedures, including those regarding domination of proceedings, and must avoid the practice or appearance of undue influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on number of federal participants
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of individual agency participants in a given voluntary standards activity should be kept to the minimum required for effective representation of program, technical, or other federal concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: If voluntary body likely to develop needed standard timely, prefer participation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a voluntary consensus standards body is likely to develop or adopt a lawful and practical standard that an agency could use in a timely fashion, the agency should not develop its own government-unique standard and should instead participate in the voluntary body's activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on conformity assessment coordination (NIST role)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 12(b) of the Act requires NIST to coordinate federal, state, and local standards and conformity assessment activities with private sector activities to eliminate unnecessary duplication and complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Secretary of Commerce must issue guidance to agencies to ensure effective coordination and to improve conformity assessment activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities of the Secretary of Commerce regarding the Circular
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of Commerce coordinates and fosters executive branch implementation of the Circular, provides administrative guidance to assist agencies (including guidance on identifying standards bodies and standards), sponsors and supports the Interagency Committee on Standards Policy (ICSP), reports to OMB on implementation, establishes procedures for public directories, and issues guidance to improve coordination on conformity assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities of Heads of Agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Heads of agencies must implement the policies of the Circular, ensure agency compliance, designate a senior official as Standards Executive for agencies with significant interest, and transmit the annual report prepared by the Agency Standards Executive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities of Agency Standards Executives
rubrics_metrics.description: An Agency Standards Executive promotes effective use of agency resources and participation and is responsible for implementation of the Circular and representation on the ICSP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Page begins listing goals and duties; agencies must prepare annual reports as described in Sections 9 and 15b(6).)
